title: WA UTC Docket 260392 — Order - Open Meeting Final: Order 01 Allowing Tariff To Go Into Effect, Subject to Conditions.
summary: Order 01 Allowing Tariff To Go Into Effect, Subject to Conditions.
text:
Service Date: June 26, 2026 

BEFORE THE WASHINGTON 
UTILITIES AND TRANSPORTATION COMMISSION 

In the Matter of the Petition of 
CARROLL-NASLUND DISPOSAL, INC. 
Petitioner, 
To Approve Tariff Revisions Regarding 
General Rates 

DOCKET TG-260392 
ORDER 01 
ALLOWING TARIFF TO GO INTO 
EFFECT, SUBJECT TO CONDITIONS
BACKGROUND 
1 
On May 14, 2026, Carroll-Naslund Disposal Service, Inc. d/b/a Naslund Disposal Service 
(Carroll-Naslund Disposal or Company) filed with the Washington Utilities and 
Transportation Commission (Commission) a general rate increase request and tariff 
revisions that would generate approximately $300,000 (14.3 percent) of additional annual 
revenue for the collection of garbage services effective July 1, 2026. The Company 
provides regulated solid waste collection service to approximately 5,200 residential, 430 
commercial, and 35 drop box customers in Asotin and Garfield Counties, Washington. 
The Company’s last general rate increase became effective on July 1, 2024. The initial 
filing indicates that the main drivers of the request are capital investments in operating 
equipment and increases in operating costs for employees, disposal, and repair expenses. 
2 
In 2026, the Company purchased two collection vehicles. One of the vehicles is a 2022 
Rear-End Loader to replace a wrecked 2011 collection vehicle, and the second is a 2026 
Automated Side Loader to improve operations. The 2011 vehicle became fully 
depreciated in 2020 but continued to be used and useful until it was inoperable and 
unable to be used for parts due to an ongoing insurance claim. The 2022 Rear-End 
Loader was acquired as a used vehicle with a depreciable life of 5 years and was put into 
service prior to the effective date in the request. 
3 
The Company is also purchasing a new 2026 Automated Side Loader to improve the 
Company’s operational efficiency, and which is not replacing any other collection 
vehicle. The new truck will have a depreciable life of 10 years, aligning with the 
Company’s longer-lived service fleet. According to the Company, this vehicle has not 
been placed into service due to manufacturer delay. The Company anticipates this vehicle 
will enter service in August or September of 2026. 

DOCKET TG-260392 

PAGE 2 
ORDER 01 

4 
The Company also acquired approximately 775 new toter containers and dumpsters as 
part of an ongoing modernization effort to increase efficiency of service. These items 
were purchased used to save costs. 
5 
On May 16, 2026, the Company notified its customers by mail of the proposed rate 
increase and of the Commission’s website where customers could access relevant 
information and contacts related to the proposed rate increase. Staff received one 
consumer comment in favor of the increase, detailing that the Company provides 
excellent customer service and understanding the reasoning for a rate increase due to 
increasing fuel prices. Staff informed the commenter that state law requires rates to be 
fair, just, reasonable, and sufficient to allow the Company to recover necessary operating 
expenses and earn a reasonable return on investment. 
6 
During Commission staff’s (Staff) review of the Company’s supporting financial 
documents, books, and records in the request in this docket 20 adjustments were made in 
addition to other adjustments by the Company during the review process. The 
adjustments include removing an employee from payroll expenses, removing expenses 
connected to non-regulated operations, reduction of repair expenses for new vehicles 
having lower wear on components in the first part of service life, removal of certain 
depreciation expenses for assets fully expired prior to the tariff effective date to avoid 
double recovery, and an update to fuel expense consistent with WAC 480-70-346. 
7 
In addition, Staff recommends that the Company hold the 2026 vehicle out of rates until 
it is received and in service, at which point the Company should then submit a 
compliance filing in this docket attesting that the vehicle is used and useful for service in 
Washington allowing a final review of the purchase price and integrating the vehicle into 
rates. The Staff otherwise believes the purchases and expenses discussed in the filing are 
necessary to modernize and run the solid waste service, cover pass-through disposal costs 
necessary and unavoidable for operation, and cover allowable repair expenses. 
8 
Staff concluded that the revised expenses are reasonable and necessary for the 
Company’s operations. The Company agreed to a revised revenue requirement of 
approximately $180,800 or 8.40 percent effective July 1, 2026, with an additional 
approximately $98,850 or 4.60 percent taking effect after receiving and placing the new 
collection vehicle in service. Staff believes the revised rates are fair, just, reasonable, and 
sufficient, and recommends approval subject to the compliance filing described above. 
9 
Staff’s Memorandum explains that the combined increase in revenue for both phases of 
the proposed rate increase, subject to compliance filing approval, would impose an 
increase of $279,600 or 13 percent of additional annual revenue, and rates would increase 

DOCKET TG-260392 

PAGE 3 
ORDER 01 

an average of 13.3 percent. For residential 64- and 96-gallon weekly service, rates would 
increase $2.78 and 3.36, respectively. Commercial rates would increase for various 
services ranging from $1.37 to $2.76, and drop box rates would increase for various 
services by $0.25 to $17.56. 
10 
Staff recommends that upon the Company filing revised tariff pages, the Commission 
allow the revised rates to take effect on July 1, 2026, subject to the following conditions: 
1) 
The Commission rejects the Tariff pages filed on May 14, 2026, directing 
the Company to file revised tariff pages for Phase 1 and Phase 2 before 
July 1, 2026. Upon filing the revised tariff pages agreed to by Commission 
Staff and Carroll-Naslund Disposal, Inc., the rates should be allowed to 
take effect July 1, 2026, excluding the 2026 Peterbilt 31-Yard Automated 
Side Loader which will not enter service until after July 1, 2026; 
2) 
The Company submit a compliance filing attesting to the Company’s 
receipt and placement into service of the 2026 Peterbilt 31 Yard 
Automated Side Loader that was reviewed but will not be received until 
after the proposed effective date; 
3) 
The Commission requires the Company to issue a notification to 
ratepayers using a bill insert in the next bill issued after the 2026 Peterbilt 
31 Yard Automated Side Loader goes into service; granting the Company 
less-than-statutory notice. The Notice should state that rates are increasing 
due to the addition of the new truck, which has been approved in Docket 
TG-260392, and should clearly state the percentage increase; and 
4) 
Requiring that if the Company submits any tariff revisions affecting rates 
filed before the effective date of the compliance period must have the 
same effective date as the tariff revisions that incorporate into rates the 
2026 Peterbilt vehicle. 
11 
This matter came before the Commission at its regularly scheduled open meeting on June 
25, 2026. Staff reiterated its position and clarified for the Commission the ongoing 
situation with the 2026 Peterbilt truck and the procedural steps needed to put that truck 
into service and into rates. The Company further explained that it was appreciative of 
Staff’s work on this case to arrive at a creative solution but explained its concerns with 
the approach resulting in customer confusion and issues with the Company’s billing 
system. The Company further explained that it does not wish to defer the tariff increases 
until the 2026 Peterbilt truck goes into service because the Company believes it would 

DOCKET TG-260392 

PAGE 4 
ORDER 01 

face significant cash flow issues. Public Counsel commented that it generally did not 
have concerns with Staff’s recommendation but raised that the Company has a pending 
insurance claim for a truck and requested the Commission require the Company to either 
file a compliance filing informing the Commission of the outcome or to file an 
accounting petition. 
DISCUSSION 
12 
The Commission agrees with Staff that the Company’s tariff revisions, adjusted and 
revised as discussed in Staff’s Memorandum, should be approved subject to the 
conditions contained in paragraph 10 of this Order. While the Commission agrees that the 
tariff rates proposed by the Company should be allowed to go into effect, we agree with 
Staff’s concerns about allowing the Company to recover in rates an asset that is not yet 
used and useful, contrary to current law. We agree that the Company should notify the 
Commission in a compliance filing attesting the Company’s receipt and placement in 
service of the 2026 Peterbilt vehicle and notify customers concurrently with the 
compliance filing of the additional increase proposed for that vehicle and that any 
additional proposed tariff revisions that have the same effective date as the tariff revisions 
incorporating the 2026 Peterbilt vehicle into rates. 
13 
Further, we agree with Public Counsel that the Commission should be made aware of the 
results of the insurance claim discussed at the open meeting. While any potential 
recovery or costs to repair remain unknown, the Commission believes it is appropriate to 
ensure that whatever the outcome, the Company have the ability to recover or provide 
back to ratepayers any costs or recovery should those fall outside of the test year for the 
Company’s next rate case. 
14 
With the conditions described above and the addition of a condition to address Public 
Counsel’s concerns, we find that the tariff revisions filed on May 14 should be rejected, 
and that the later revised tariff pages, to be filed before July 1, 2026, are fair, just, 
reasonable, and sufficient, and may go into effect on July 1, 2026, subject to the 
conditions contained in paragraph 18 of this Order. 
FINDINGS AND CONCLUSIONS 
15 
(1) 
The Commission is an agency of the State of Washington vested by statute with 
the authority to regulate the rates, regulations, practices, accounts, and affiliated 
interests of public service companies, including solid waste companies. 

DOCKET TG-260392 

PAGE 5 
ORDER 01 

16 
(2) 
Carroll-Naslund is engaged in the business of providing solid waste services 
within the State of Washington and is a public service company subject to 
Commission jurisdiction. 
17 
(3) 
This matter came before the Commission at its regularly scheduled meeting on 
June 25, 2026. 
18 
(4) 
After review of the tariff revisions filed in Docket TG-260392 by Carroll-Naslund 
on May 14, 2026, and later revised, and giving due consideration, the 
Commission finds that the tariff revisions should be granted subject to the 
following conditions: 
1) 
The Commission rejects the Tariff pages filed on May 14, 2026, and 
directs the Company to file revised tariff pages for Phase 1 and Phase 2 
before July 1, 2026. Upon filing the revised tariff pages agreed to by 
Commission Staff and Carroll-Naslund Disposal, Inc., the rates are 
allowed to take effect July 1, 2026, excluding the 2026 Peterbilt 31-Yard 
Automated Side Loader which will not enter service until after July 1, 
2026; 
2) 
Before the 2026 Peterbilt 31-yard Automated Side Loader can be placed 
into rates, the Company must submit a compliance filing attesting to the 
Company’s receipt and placement into service of the 2026 Peterbilt 31 
Yard Automated Side Loader that Staff reviewed but the Company did not 
receive until after the proposed effective date; 
3) 
The Commission requires the Company to issue a notification to 
ratepayers using a bill insert in the next bill issued after the 2026 Peterbilt 
31 Yard Automated Side Loader goes into service. The Notice must state 
that rates are increasing due to the addition of the new truck, which has 
been approved in Docket TG-260392, and should clearly state the 
percentage increase; 
4) 
Granting the Company less-than-statutory treatment of the notice and 
effect of the compliance filing in relation to placing the 2026 Peterbilt into 
service; 
5) 
Requiring that if the Company submits any tariff revisions affecting rates 
filed before the effective date of the compliance period; those revisions 

DOCKET TG-260392 

PAGE 6 
ORDER 01 

must have the same effective date as the tariff revisions that incorporate 
into rates the 2026 Peterbilt vehicle; and 
6) 
Requiring the Company to file with the Commission a petition for 
accounting deferral once the Company learns of the resolution of the 
pending insurance claim. 
ORDER 
THE COMMISSION ORDERS: 
19 
(1) 
The tariff revisions filed by Carroll-Naslund Disposal Service, Inc. d/b/a Naslund 
Disposal Service filed May 14, 2026, are rejected and shall be revised before July 
1, 2026, as agreed to by the parties, and that the revisions agreed to are fair, just, 
reasonable, and sufficient, and may go into effect on July 1, 2026, subject to the 
following conditions: 
1) 
The Commission rejects the Tariff pages filed on May 14, 2026, and 
directs the Company to file revised tariff pages for Phase 1 and Phase 2 
before July 1, 2026. Upon filing the revised tariff pages agreed to by Staff 
and Carroll-Naslund Disposal, Inc., the rates are allowed to take effect 
July 1, 2026, excluding the 2026 Peterbilt 31-Yard Automated Side 
Loader, which will not enter service until after July 1, 2026; 
2) 
Before the 2026 Peterbilt 31-yard Automated Side Loader can be placed 
into rates, the Company must submit a compliance filing attesting to the 
Company’s receipt and placement into service of the 2026 Peterbilt 31 
Yard Automated Side Loader that Staff reviewed but the Company did not 
receive until after the proposed effective date; 
3) 
The Commission requires the Company to issue a notification to 
ratepayers using a bill insert in the next bill issued after the 2026 Peterbilt 
31 Yard Automated Side Loader goes into service. The Notice must state 
that rates are increasing due to the addition of the new truck, which has 
been approved in Docket TG-260392, and should clearly state the 
percentage increase; 
4) 
Granting the Company less-than-statutory treatment of the notice and 
effect of the compliance filing in relation to placing the 2026 Peterbilt into 
service; 

DOCKET TG-260392 

PAGE 7 
ORDER 01 

5) 
Requiring that if the Company submits any tariff revisions affecting rates 
filed before the effective date of the compliance period, those revisions 
must have the same effective date as the tariff revisions that incorporate 
into rates the 2026 Peterbilt vehicle; and 
6) 
Requiring the Company to file with the Commission a petition for 
accounting deferral once the Company learns of the resolution of the 
pending insurance claim. 
20 
(2) 
The Commission authorizes the Commission Secretary to accept by letter a filing 
that complies with the requirements of this Order. 
21 
(3) 
The Commission retains jurisdiction over the subject matter and Carroll-Naslund 
Disposal Service, Inc. d/b/a Naslund Disposal Service to effectuate the provisions 
of this Order. 
DATED at Lacey, Washington, June 26, 2026. 
WASHINGTON UTILITIES AND TRANSPORTATION COMMISSION 
BRIAN RYBARIK, Chair 
ANN E. RENDAHL, Commissioner 
MILTON H. DOUMIT, Commissioner
